mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying {فِيهِ ذكركُمْ}: الذّكر is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and {فِيهِ} the khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying, the Exalted, {من ذكر من رَبهم مُحدث}: مُحدث is a naʿt (adjective) of الذّكر. Al-Kisāʾī permitted it in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and al-Farrāʾ permitted it in the nominative as a naʿt of ذكر according to its position, because مِن is redundant (zāʾida) and ذكر is the fāʿil (agent).

mekki-muskil:22-22.t:
His saying {لَو كَانَ فيهمَا آلِهَة إِلَّا الله}: إلا is in the place of غير, and it is a naʿt (adjective) of آلهة according to Sībawayh and al-Kisāʾī, its implied form being "other than Allah" (غير الله). Since إِلَّا was put in the place of غير, the noun after it was inflected with the same inflection as غير. Al-Farrāʾ said: إِلَّا has the meaning of سوى.
Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read هَذَا ذكرٌ مَن معي وَذكرٌ مَن قبلي with tanwīn, on the assumption of an omission, its implied form being "this is a reminder, the reminder of those with me and the reminder of those before me" (هَذِه ذكر ذكر من معي وَذكر من قبلي).

mekki-muskil:24-24.t: His saying {الْحق}: accusative by يعلمون. Al-Ḥasan read it in the nominative in the meaning "it is the truth" (هُوَ الْحق) or "this is the truth" (هذا الحق).

mekki-muskil:26-26.t: His saying {بل عباد مكرمون}: i.e. "rather they are honoured servants" (بل هم عباد), a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). Al-Farrāʾ permitted بل عبادا مكرمين in the meaning "rather He took honoured servants" (بل اتخذ عبادا).

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying {وأسروا النَّجْوَى الَّذين ظلمُوا}: الَّذين is a badal (substitute) from the latent nominative pronoun in أَسرُّوا, and the pronoun refers back to النَّاس. It is said that الَّذين is nominative by implying "they are those who…" (هم الَّذين); and it is said that الَّذين is in the position of the accusative by [an implied] "I mean" (أَعنِي). Al-Farrāʾ permitted الَّذين to be in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of النَّاس. It is said that الَّذين is nominative by أسروا, and the pronoun form in أَسرُّوا came according to the dialect of those who say أكلوني البراغيث ("the fleas ate me", with a plural marker on the verb before an overt plural agent). And it is said that الَّذين is nominative by implying "says" (يَقُول).

mekki-muskil:30-30.t:
His saying {كَانَتَا رتقا}: رتقا was made singular only because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "the two were possessors of closure" (كَانَتَا ذواتي رتق).
His saying {وَجَعَلنَا من المَاء كل شَيْء حَيّ}: من المَاء is in the position of the second object of جعل. It is permissible in ordinary speech to read حَيا in the accusative as the second object, and من المَاء would then be in the position of clarification (bayān).

mekki-muskil:33-33.t: His saying {فِي فلك يسبحون}: يسبحون came with the wāw and nūn [of the masculine sound plural], although it is predicated of things that are not rational. The rule for the wāw and nūn is that they are only for the rational; but since it was said of them that they perform an action, just as is said of the rational, the predication about them came like the predication about the rational.

mekki-muskil:34-34.t: His saying {أَفَإِن مت فهم الخالدون}: the rule for the interrogative alif, when it enters upon a conditional particle, is that its rank is before the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); so the meaning is "will they then be the immortal ones, if you die?" (أفهم الخالدون إِن مت). Like it is {أَفَإِن مَاتَ أَو قتل انقلبتم}, and this is frequent.

mekki-muskil:47-47.t:
His saying {وَإِن كَانَ مِثْقَال حَبَّة}: whoever reads مثقال in the nominative makes كان complete (tāmma), not needing a khabar. Whoever reads it in the accusative makes كان deficient (nāqiṣa), so it is its khabar, and the noun of كان is implied in it, its implied form being "and even if the wrong is the weight of a grain" (وَإِن كَانَ الظُّلم مِثْقَال حَبَّة); since the wrong was mentioned before, implying it is permissible.
His saying {أَتَيْنَا بهَا}: whoever reads it short (أَتَيْنا) — its meaning is "We bring it". Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid read آتينا with madd (lengthening), in the meaning "We requite with it", so it is on the pattern فاعلنا. It is not good for it to be أفعلنا, because that would require dropping the bāʾ from بها, since أفعل [in this sense] does not take its object through a preposition, and dropping the bāʾ contradicts the script.

mekki-muskil:52-52.t: His saying {إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ}: the governing word (ʿāmil) of إذ is آتينا [in] "We gave Ibrāhīm", i.e. "We gave him his right guidance at the time he said to his father".

mekki-muskil:60-60.t: His saying {يُقَال لَهُ إِبْرَاهِيم}: إبراهيم is nominative by implying "he is Ibrāhīm" (هُوَ إبراهيم), a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) reported (maḥkī). It is also said that its implied form is "the one by whom he is known is Ibrāhīm" (الَّذِي يعرف بِهِ إبراهيم). And it is said that it is nominative as a singular vocative (munādā mufrad), so its ḍamma is one of indeclinability (bināʾ); and له stands in place of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of يقال. Or, if you wish, you imply the maṣdar (verbal noun) to stand in place of the agent, and له is then in the position of the accusative.

mekki-muskil:74-74.t: His saying {ولوطا آتيناه}: لوطا is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "and We gave Lūṭ — We gave him…" (وآتينا لوطا آتيناه). After it {نوحًا} and {دَاوُد} are accusative in the meaning "and mention, O Muḥammad, Nūḥ, and mention Dāwūd".

mekki-muskil:79-79.t: His saying {وَالطير}: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الْجبَال; and it is said to be a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). The nominative is permissible, conjoining it to the latent pronoun in {يسبحْنَ}.

mekki-muskil:87-87.t: His saying {إِذْ ذهب مغاضبا}: مغاضبا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Its meaning is that he was angry with his people for the sake of his Lord, since his people did not respond to him; and the anger at the people was because of their opposing the command of their Lord.

mekki-muskil:109-109.t:
His saying {آذنتكم على سَوَاء}: {على سَوَاء} may be in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a notification on equal terms" (إيذانا على سَوَاء). It may also be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent, who is the Prophet ﷺ, or from the objects, who are those addressed. Like it in permissibility is His saying {فانبذ إِلَيْهِم على سَوَاء}, in the position of a ḥāl from the Prophet ﷺ and from the unbelievers, i.e. being equal in the knowledge of the breaking of the covenant. This is like their saying لَقِي زيد عمرا ضاحكين ("Zayd met ʿAmr, both laughing"), and like the poet's saying:
... فلئن لقيتك خاليين لتعلمن ...
(If I meet you, the two of us alone, you will surely know …)
So خاليين is a ḥāl from the tāʾ and from the kāf; and there is disagreement about it because of the difference between the two governing words of the two possessors of the ḥāl.

mekki-muskil:88-88.t:
His saying {ننجي الْمُؤمنِينَ}: Ibn ʿĀmir, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, read it with one nūn and a doubled jīm (نُجِّي). The yāʾ should then have had fatḥa, because it is a past passive verb, and الْمُؤمنِينَ should be nominative on this reading, because it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of a past passive verb. But it came on the basis of implying the maṣdar (verbal noun), which he set up in place of the agent; and that is remote, because the object has the better right to stand in place of the agent, and the maṣdar stands in place of the agent only in the absence of a direct object, or when the direct object is occupied by a preposition, e.g. قيم وسير بزيد ("there was a standing and a journeying with Zayd"). As for the yāʾ, he made it quiescent in the place of fatḥa, just as he makes it quiescent in the place of the nominative; and that too is remote — it is permitted only in poetry.
Some of the scholars said that نجي in this reading is not a verb whose agent is named [i.e. not a passive], but that the second nūn was assimilated into the jīm. This too is a remote view, because the nūn is not assimilated into the jīm with a true assimilation that produces doubling; it is only concealed (ikhfāʾ) before the jīm, and concealment does not bring doubling.
ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: in this reading it is an active verb, and its origin is ننجي with two nūns and doubling on the pattern نُفَعِّل, but the second nūn was dropped because of the meeting of the two nūns, as one of the two tāʾs was dropped in تفرقون and تظاهرون and the like. Those who held these last two views used as evidence for their view the quiescence of the yāʾ in ننجي, its quiescence indicating that it is an imperfect verb. This too is a weak view, because with two identical letters in such cases the second is dropped for lightness only when the vowels of the two identical letters agree, e.g. تتفرقون and تتعاونون; if the vowels of the two identical letters differ, dropping the second is not permitted, e.g. تتغافر الذُّنُوب and تتناتج الدَّوَابّ. The vowels of the two nūns in ننجي differ, so dropping is not permitted at all in either of them. Moreover, the second nūn is radical, and a radical letter may not be dropped at all; whereas the tāʾ dropped in {تفَرقُوا} and {وتعاونوا} is an augment, so dropping it is good when the two vowels agree.

mekki-muskil:90-90.t: His saying {رغبا ورهبا}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:91-91.t:
His saying {وَالَّتِي أحصنت}: الَّتِي is in the position of the accusative in the meaning "and mention the one who…" (وَاذْكُر الَّتِي); and likewise {وَذَا النُّون}.
His saying {وجعلناها وَابْنهَا آيَة للْعَالمين}: آيَة is the second object of جعل, and it was not made dual because the implied form according to Sībawayh is "and We made her a sign for the worlds, and We made her son a sign" (وجعلناها آيَة للْعَالمين وَجَعَلنَا ابْنهَا آيَة); then the first was omitted because the second indicates it. Its implied form according to al-Mubarrad involves no omission, but fronting is intended; its implied form according to him is "and We made her a sign for the worlds, and her son" (وجعلناها آيَة للْعَالمين وَابْنهَا).

mekki-muskil:96-96.t: His saying {حَتَّى إِذا فتحت يَأْجُوج وَمَأْجُوج}: the answer of إذا is omitted, and the meaning is "they said {يَا ويلنا}", and the verb "said" was omitted. It is also said that its answer is {واقترب الْوَعْد الْحق}, the wāw being redundant (zāʾida); and it is said that its answer is {فَإِذا هِيَ شاخصة}.
